newsitem.title: USA: Woman testifies she was raped by US Army sergeant.
newsitem.headline: Woman testifies she was raped by US Army sergeant.

text.p: The first woman trainee to testify at the court-martial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson said he forced her onto a bed and raped her when she tried to complain about how he was picking on her.

The woman, whose name was not made public, was the first alleged victim to testify at the court-martial, which is the highest-profile case in the growing Army sex scandal in which 11 other drill sergeants have been charged.
She also said she had consensual sex with two other drill sergeants. It is against Army regulations for a drill sergeant to have sex with a trainee.
Another woman trainee testified she was a victim of an unsolicited kiss by Simpson and described a climate of sexual promiscuity among Army drill sergeants.

"After the first two weeks there were rumours going around about people having sex with drill sergeants, about persons sneaking around with this person and this person is fine," the second woman said.

Simpson, 32, faces 19 counts of rape and 39 other charges including indecent exposure, battery and maltreatment involving 13 women. He has pleaded innocent to the charges but earlier pleaded guilty to 11 counts of improper sexual intercourse with trainees and five counts of propositioning.

The alleged acts occurred in 1995 and 1996, while Simpson was a drill instructor at the Ordnance Centre and School at the Aberdeen Proving Ground, overseeing classes of five to 45 soldiers receiving advanced instruction after basic training.

The alleged rape victim, who was 20 at the time, said Simpson had criticised her for wearing nail polish, which she said she told him was not against regulations. She said Simpson continued to pick on her and finally she decided to confront him, so she went to his office and "told him off."
"He just kind of leaned back in the chair and laughed," she said. Then he got up, came around the desk and said he knew she had had an affair with another drill sergeant, the woman testified.

She said his back was to the door and he came toward her and grabbed her by the arms and kissed her on the face and neck. She said he then pushed her backwards through a door into another room and onto a bed.
"He put my hands above my head and I told him 'no.' I was crying," she testified. But she said Simpson unbuttoned her shirt and fondled her breasts, then pulled down her pants and raped her.

"I didn't know what he was going to do because he was so mean -- beat me, hit me, kill me," she said. Afterwards, she said, Simpson again warned her he knew about her affair with the other sergeant and said if she told anybody that he had raped her nobody would believe her.
She said she waited two weeks before she told a sergeant who told her he was concerned about a change in her attitude. She said she then had sexual relations with that sergeant.
"It was embarrasing. I didn't think anybody would believe me," she said.
The second woman to testify said she did not consider Simpson's kiss a sexual assault. "I wasn't offended. I was basically shocked. If I was offended I would have told somebody."

Simpson's attorneys have said their client engaged only in consensual sex. "A number of female soldiers in training were attracted to and willingly engaged in sexual intercourse with Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson," defence attorney Capt. Edward Brady said in his opening statement last week.

Brady said Army investigators used excessive zeal in interviewing witnesses. "Their own witnesses will tell you that (investigators) actively encouraged them to embellish their statements ... to 'make it jucier,'" he said.
